thread.title: Bull trend grinds higher, S&P 500 extends January breakout - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Bull trend grinds higher, S&P 500 extends January breakout - MarketWatch
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the U.S. benchmarks’ broadly-based bull trend continues to grind higher.
On a headline basis, each big three benchmark has notched consecutive record closes, a move technically neutralizing last week’s respectable mid-month downdraft.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +0.22% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has extended its uptrend, notching another record high.
Tactically, first support (2,807) matches the former range top. Delving deeper, a near-term floor, circa 2,774, underpinned last week’s fleeting downturn.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has edged less decisively to record territory.
Still, the slight breakout is constructive. The blue-chip benchmark has registered four straight closes atop the 26,000 mark.
From current levels, the breakout point (26,150) pivots to first support, and is followed by a very near-term floor, circa 25,940.
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.68% has also registered another record high.
Tactically, the 7,330 area remains an inflection point, and is followed by a deeper floor, circa 7,220.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has knifed decisively to record territory. Though stubbornly near-term extended, the nearly straightline January rally is longer-term bullish.
Recall that the ascending 20-day moving average, currently 7,146, is closely followed by support, circa 7,110, matching a weekly low.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has also taken flight.
The chart above includes the 20-day Bollinger bands, also known as volatility bands. As always, the bands bracket two standard deviations of the Dow’s trailing 20-day volatility.
Recall that consecutive closes atop the bands signal an increasingly familiar technical tension.
Specifically, such closes signal a near-term extended posture — due at least a sideways chopping-around phase — against a firmly-bullish longer-term backdrop.
The Dow’s January breakout has encompassed six closes atop the bands across a nine-session span. This is statistically unusual, and distinctly bullish for the longer-term.
The index previously registered precisely five consecutive closes atop the bands, price action preceding the strong January spike. (See the late-July, September and November breakouts.)
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is also trending firmly higher.
The prevailing breakout punctuates the late-December bull flag, and has encompassed five recent closes atop the 20-day volatility bands.
The bigger picture The major U.S. benchmarks have taken flight to start the new year, and selling pressure near record highs remains muted.
Each widely-tracked benchmark has recently confirmed its primary uptrend.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF’s IWM, +0.34% backdrop has weathered a potentially bearish pattern, a key reversal, detailed last week.
As illustrated, the small-cap benchmark has maintained first support (155.80), subsequently rising to register consecutive record closes.
Meanwhile, the S&P MidCap 400 has also notched consecutive record closes. In its case, support spans from 249.20 to 530.40, the latter closely matching the mid-month low.
Similarly, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 has extended its uptrend.
Recall that the mid-month pullback was fueled by decreased volume, and punctuated by a stronger-volume extension. Constructive price action.
Summing up the backdrop All told, the bigger-picture backdrop remains straightforward and comfortably bullish.
As it applies to the S&P 500, the index has absorbed the mid-January whipsaw — the downdraft to the 2,775 area — and reversed swiftly to another record high.
The ascending 20-day moving average, currently 2,747 (not illustrated), is rising toward support, and the S&P’s near-term uptrend is intact barring a violation.
Beyond technical levels, the primary bull trend remains broadly-based, firmly-grounded and underpinned by healthy sector rotation. All trends technically point higher pending signs of a bearish pulse.
See also: January breakout accelerates, S&P 500 clears 20-day volatility bands.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Profiled last week, the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF GDX, +0.21% is acting well technically.
As illustrated, the group has recently knifed to four-month highs, rising from a successful test of the 200-day moving average. (The 200-day has marked a bull-bear inflection point. See the September low, and November range top.)
The ensuing pullback has been comparably flat, fueled by decreased volume, preserving a bullish bias.
Tactically, the former range top, circa 23.80, is followed by the 200-day moving average, currently 22.80. The group’s rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
Moving to specific names, Newmont Mining Corp. is a well positioned large-cap gold miner.
Late last month, the shares cleared trendline resistance, rising to challenge overhead matching 16-month highs.
The subsequent tight one-week range signals muted selling pressure at resistance, improving the chances of eventual follow-through. Near-term support (38.90) closely matches last week’s low, and a breakout attempt is in play barring a violation.
Looking elsewhere, Synaptics, Inc. SYNA, -1.37% is a mid-cap developer of touchpads and other human-interface technologies.
As illustrated, the shares have recently gapped atop the 200-day moving average, rising after the company’s new in-display fingerprint sensor induced an analyst upgrade.
The subsequent pullback has been fueled by decreased volume, placing the shares at an attractive entry near the breakout point and 12.7% under the January peak. The post-breakout low (43.85) closely matches support, and the rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
Activision Blizzard, Inc. ATVI, +0.59% is a large-cap video game developer positioned to rise.
The shares initially spiked two weeks ago, reaching all-time highs after the company’s Overwatch League debut.
The ensuing bull flag is a continuation pattern, positioning the shares to extend the January rally. First support matches the breakout point, circa 67.50, and a posture higher supports a bullish bias.
KB Home KBH, +0.26% is a well positioned mid-cap homebuilder.
Technically, the shares have recently gapped to 10-year highs, rising after the company’s strong fourth-quarter results.
The ensuing pullback has been orderly, placing the shares at an attractive entry near the bottom of the gap, and 10.8% under the January peak. Consider that the ascending 20-day moving average, currently 34.00, has defined the prevailing uptrend.
Initially profiled Jan. 12, Vuzix Corp. VUZI, +0.00% has returned 8.2% and remains well positioned.
As illustrated, the shares started January with a breakout, rising after the company announced it would release augmented-reality glasses designed to support Amazon’s Alexa at the Consumer Electronics Show.
The subsequent pullback has been underpinned by the bottom of the gap, and punctuated by a 52-week closing peak.
Tactically, the prevailing range top (9.55) closely matches major resistance illustrated on the three-year chart. A near-term target projects to the 11.20 area on follow-through.
